root_cause: CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race spawns multiple concurrent threads that race to load/cache a model and asserts the mock plugin's import_model() is called exactly 3 times. On Windows runners, thread scheduling occasionally lets one thread observe the cache file before another thread finishes writing it, so only 2 of the 3 expected cache-miss imports occur, making the GMock EXPECT_CALL count assertion fail. This is an existing known timing-sensitive (racy) test unrelated to the PR being merged (#40203), which only touched a single CMake option (ENABLE_STATIC_LIBS_PDB) in src/CMakeLists.txt and does not affect the caching test or ICompiledModel import_model logic.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally; requires running src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp's CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race/ByModelName_testCache repeatedly (e.g., in a loop with --gtest_repeat=200 --gtest_filter=CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race*) on a loaded Windows CI-like machine to trigger the race window.
recommended_actions: Increase the race-test's retry/tolerance window in caching_test.cpp around line 2673 so a 2-vs-3 call count during the race does not immediately fail, or add a short synchronization barrier between cache-writer and cache-reader threads before asserting call counts.
Consider marking CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race as a known-flaky test on Windows (e.g., via test filter/skip list) until the underlying race condition is fixed.
No action needed on PR #40203 itself — the merged change (ENABLE_STATIC_LIBS_PDB CMake fix) is unrelated to this test failure.
prevention_strategies: Add deterministic synchronization (e.g., explicit thread join points or condition variables) around the mock-call-count assertions in multi-threaded caching race tests instead of relying on timing to guarantee call counts. Track recurring flaky-test signatures in the CI Doctor pattern DB and auto-quarantine tests once they exceed a recurrence threshold.
historical_context: This exact signature has recurred 4 times before (2026-11-09, 2026-11-20, 2026-11-20, 2026-11-21) across unrelated commits, confirming it is a long-standing flaky test rather than a regression introduced by this commit.
